Compare schemes, weights and ties

Source: vignettes/choosing-cv.Rmd
choosing-cv.Rmd

A selection rule compares candidate CV schemes for the same target and final prediction model. It seeks a useful estimate of that model’s target MSE. It does not seek the smallest CV score.

Specify candidates and a weighted target 

set.seed(101)
training <- matrix(runif(120), ncol = 2)
q <- as.matrix(expand.grid(x = seq(0.1, 1.3, length.out = 8),
                          y = seq(0.1, 0.9, length.out = 8)))
target <- prediction_target(q, weights = ifelse(q[, 1] > 1, 2, 1),
                            label = "Target with extra weight beyond the sampled region")
schemes <- list(
  random = spatial_folds(training, 5, "random", seed = 4),
  block = spatial_folds(training, 5, "block", seed = 4),
  buffered = spatial_folds(training, 5, "buffered", buffer = 0.04, seed = 4)
)
model <- spatial_covariance(range = 0.2, signal = 0.8)

The buffer removes training observations within 0.04 coordinate units of a test observation. If this empties a training set, the constructor reports an error; reduce the buffer or reconsider the partition. Matching seeds gives block and buffered schemes the same test groups.

Compare two selection criteria 

by_W <- compare_cv_schemes(training, schemes, target, model, criterion = "W")
by_J2 <- compare_cv_schemes(training, schemes, target, model, criterion = "J2")
by_W
#> CV comparison by W 
#>    scheme         W         J2 criterion_value selection_probability
#>    random 0.1005988  0.1171102       0.1005988                   0.0
#>     block 0.0730827 -0.1249033       0.0730827                   0.5
#>  buffered 0.0730827 -0.1249033       0.0730827                   0.5
by_J2
#> CV comparison by |J2| 
#>    scheme         W         J2 criterion_value selection_probability
#>    random 0.1005988  0.1171102       0.1171102                     1
#>     block 0.0730827 -0.1249033       0.1249033                     0
#>  buffered 0.0730827 -0.1249033       0.1249033                     0

W measures a distance-distribution discrepancy. abs(J2) compares average squared correlation and can allow cancellation. They need not select the same scheme. A single common covariance specification is used for all candidates.

If covariance is estimated from observed training responses, pass an estimate_covariance(training, response) result in place of model. Selection then depends on those responses. The covariance used to make each held-out prediction should still be estimated from that fold’s training data only.

Add kNNDM when appropriate

kNNDM is a candidate CV construction, whereas W and J2 are criteria that can evaluate it alongside the other candidates. The optional constructor uses the implementation in CAST. It currently constructs folds for equally weighted target points. For a weighted target you may audit externally supplied folds, but the CAST construction itself does not optimise those weights.

install.packages(c("sf", "CAST"))
equal_target <- prediction_target(q)
schemes$knndm <- spatial_folds(training, 5, "knndm",
                              target = equal_target, seed = 4)
compare_cv_schemes(training, schemes, equal_target, model, criterion = "J2")

Evaluate a rule when the generating distribution is known

In a simulation, gaussian_cv() can calculate expected CV MSE and target MSE without simulating responses. This example assumes the known-mean Gaussian model with the covariance specified above. All schemes share the same target MSE.

reference <- lapply(schemes, function(f) gaussian_cv(training, f, target, model))
evaluation <- data.frame(
  scheme = names(schemes),
  target_mse = vapply(reference, `[[`, numeric(1), "target_mse"),
  cv_mse = vapply(reference, `[[`, numeric(1), "cv_mse"),
  absolute_bias = abs(vapply(reference, `[[`, numeric(1), "optimism"))
)
evaluation
#>            scheme target_mse    cv_mse absolute_bias
#> random     random  0.7183768 0.5756394     0.1427374
#> block       block  0.7183768 0.8796564     0.1612796
#> buffered buffered  0.7183768 0.8796564     0.1612796

The best scheme by absolute_bias is the one whose expected CV MSE is closest to target MSE. Target MSE is used here only for evaluation, after the diagnostic choices were made. In an application it is not usually known.

Handle ties without using target errors 

same <- list(first = schemes$random, second = schemes$random)
tied <- compare_cv_schemes(training, same, target, model)
tied$table[, c("scheme", "criterion_value", "selection_probability")]
#>   scheme criterion_value selection_probability
#> 1  first       0.1171102                   0.5
#> 2 second       0.1171102                   0.5

If two schemes tie, a rule that chooses uniformly between them has expected evaluation loss equal to the average of their individual losses. For example, signed estimation errors −0.1-0.1 and 0.10.1 give average absolute error 0.1. Averaging the signed errors first would give zero and would assess a different estimator.

sum(by_J2$table$selection_probability * evaluation$absolute_bias)
#> [1] 0.1427374

The default absolute tie tolerance is 10−1210^{-12} in criterion units. Report and check that tolerance when very weak correlation makes all contrasts tiny. With zero spatial signal, all J2 values are zero and all candidates tie.
